description: Excited to participate in the Dancing with the SARs challenge! Seeking members with experience in change detection, APIs, satellite imagery, data science, and general synthetic aperture radar. Extended experience with Python preferable.
summary:
Delta-Earth is an interactive Earth observation platform that transforms complex satellite radar data into accessible visualizations and compelling environmental stories. Developed using NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) data.
Recognizing the enormous size and complexity of satellite datasets, we developed an efficient data-processing architecture integrating NASA Earthdata, ASF, and Harmony services. Instead of downloading massive satellite products, our system retrieves geographically targeted subsets, enabling users to explore regions worldwide through an interactive 3D globe.
Built with React, CesiumJS, and FastAPI, Delta-Earth provides interactive temporal visualizations, radar backscatter analysis, pixel-level inspection, and observation comparisons. Our change-detection tools help users investigate environmental transformations across different acquisition dates.
Beyond technical analysis, we introduced an interactive storytelling system connecting satellite observations with real-world environmental events. Our featured case study explores the Ganga River's changing floodplain near Bhagalpur, India, during the 2026 monsoon season.
Designed for scalability and accessibility, Delta-Earth bridges the gap between scientific radar observations and public understanding, empowering researchers, educators, decision-makers, and communities to explore Earth's evolving landscape.
details:
What Does It Do?

Delta-Earth, developed by Team E=mc² + AI for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, is an interactive Earth observation platform that transforms NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) data into accessible visualizations and environmental stories.

Our platform allows users to explore Earth's changing surface through interactive maps, satellite observation timelines, radar comparisons, and real-world environmental case studies.

Key Features

Interactive 3D Earth Exploration

Explore locations worldwide using a CesiumJS-powered 3D globe. Users can draw custom geographic polygons to select areas for satellite analysis.

Automated NISAR Observation Discovery

Delta-Earth integrates NASA Earthdata, CMR, and ASF services to discover available NISAR observations, acquisition dates, and metadata for selected regions.

Efficient Satellite Data Retrieval

Using NASA Harmony, our platform retrieves geographic subsets of satellite observations instead of downloading enormous source products, reducing data transfer and storage requirements.

Interactive Temporal Visualization

An interactive timeline lets users navigate NISAR observations across different dates, revealing changes in radar backscatter through consistent visualization settings.

Radar Analysis and Change Detection

Users can inspect radar values, adjust color palettes, compare observations side by side, and visualize raster differences to investigate potential surface changes.

Interactive Environmental Storytelling

Our Story Explorer connects satellite observations with environmental events through clickable globe markers, guided narratives, and interactive timelines.

Featured Case Study — Bihar Floods 2026

"When the Ganga Overflowed" explores apparent floodplain changes near Bhagalpur, Bihar, using eight NISAR observations acquired between June and October 2026.

How Does It Work?

Delta-Earth connects a React frontend, FastAPI backend, and NASA Earth observation services through an automated geospatial workflow.

Step 1 — Select Region: Users draw a polygon on the interactive 3D globe.

Step 2 — Discover Observations: The backend searches NASA CMR and ASF for available NISAR acquisitions.

Step 3 — Extract Data: NASA Harmony provides geographic subsets of selected observations.

Step 4 — Process Rasters: Extracted GeoTIFF files are validated, organized, and stored for visualization.

Step 5 — Visualize Changes: Users explore acquisition timelines, radar imagery, pixel values, and observation comparisons.

Step 6 — Explore Stories: Environmental case studies connect satellite observations with real-world geographic events.

System Architecture

What Makes It Innovative?

Efficient Processing of Massive Satellite Datasets

Instead of downloading entire NISAR products, Delta-Earth integrates NASA Harmony's geographic subsetting capabilities into an interactive workflow, making regional analysis more practical.

Scientific Visualization Meets Storytelling

Delta-Earth combines radar analysis tools with interactive environmental narratives, making the same satellite observations useful for scientific exploration and public education.

Explore Anywhere on Earth

Unlike applications restricted to predefined locations, users can select custom geographic regions and discover available NISAR observations.

Interactive Change Exploration

Timeline navigation, observation comparisons, and raster difference maps help users investigate how radar measurements change across acquisition dates.

Scalable Environmental Story Library

Our reusable storytelling framework supports additional locations and environmental events without requiring a separate application for every case study.

Impact and Benefits

Researchers and Environmental Scientists

Simplifies NISAR observation discovery, geographic extraction, and temporal comparison, providing an accessible starting point for investigating surface changes.

Disaster Monitoring and Environmental Management

Demonstrates how radar observations can support investigations of floods and other environmental disturbances, with potential applications in disaster assessment after further validation.

Students and Educators

Transforms complex satellite radar measurements into interactive learning experiences through maps, timelines, comparisons, and environmental stories.

Communities and the General Public

Makes Earth observation more accessible, helping people explore environmental changes affecting locations and communities around the world.

Intended Impact

Our goal is to bridge the gap between advanced satellite technology and public understanding, encouraging environmental awareness, scientific exploration, and collaborative research.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software

Frontend and Visualization

  • React: Interactive user interface.
  • TypeScript / JavaScript: Application functionality.
  • CesiumJS: 3D Earth visualization.
  • HTML / CSS: Interface design.
  • Raster Visualization: Satellite imagery and temporal comparisons.

Backend and Geospatial Processing

  • Python: Backend development.
  • FastAPI: REST APIs and processing workflows.
  • Rasterio / GDAL: Geospatial raster processing.
  • GeoTIFF: Satellite raster storage.
  • JSON / GeoJSON: Metadata and geographic information.

NASA Data and Services

  • NASA-ISRO NISAR: Primary radar observation source.
  • NASA Earthdata: Earth observation infrastructure.
  • NASA CMR: Satellite observation discovery.
  • Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF): NISAR data catalog.
  • NASA Harmony: Geographic data subsetting.

Development and Collaboration

  • Git / GitHub: Version control and collaboration.
  • Visual Studio Code: Development and debugging.
  • Web Browsers: Application testing.

Hardware

Delta-Earth is browser-based and requires no specialized satellite-processing hardware on the user's device.

Factors Considered During Development

Data Efficiency: Minimize unnecessary downloads and storage through geographic subsetting and reusable raster products.

Scientific Accuracy: Distinguish observable radar backscatter differences from scientifically validated environmental classifications.

Temporal Consistency: Maintain comparable visualization settings across satellite acquisition dates.

Accessibility: Provide intuitive tools for beginners while retaining detailed analysis capabilities.

Scalability: Support additional geographic regions, observations, and environmental stories.

User Experience: Simplify complex satellite-data workflows through an interactive web interface.

Potential Considerations and Future Directions

Automated Environmental Classification

Develop validated algorithms for identifying flooding, vegetation disturbance, and other environmental changes from radar observations.

Additional Earth Observation Data

Integrate Sentinel imagery, optical observations, rainfall records, and river-gauge measurements to improve environmental interpretation.

Quantitative Change Analysis

Introduce validated measurements of flood extent, land-cover variation, and other environmental indicators.

Advanced Radar Analysis

Expand support for polarization comparisons, acquisition geometry analysis, and additional satellite measurements.

Global Environmental Story Library

Extend our case studies to Amazon deforestation, wildfires, glacier movement, coastal changes, and agricultural transformations.

Actionable Environmental Insights

Develop tools that could support environmental monitoring, education, disaster assessment, and evidence-based decision-making.

E=mc² + AI — Team Workflow & Planning

Our team organized development into research, technical feasibility, architecture design, implementation, integration, testing, and presentation.

Research and Planning

We studied NISAR's capabilities, NASA's available datasets, and potential environmental case studies to identify suitable applications for radar-based change visualization.

Technical Feasibility

After encountering the limitations of downloading massive satellite products, we redesigned our architecture around NASA Harmony's geographic subsetting services.

Development and Integration

We developed interconnected components for data retrieval, geospatial visualization, temporal analysis, environmental storytelling, and user interface design.

Testing and Refinement

We iteratively addressed data retrieval failures, asynchronous processing, raster validation, geographic accuracy, and visualization consistency.

Final Presentation

We prepared interactive demonstrations, technical documentation, and environmental case studies to communicate the platform's capabilities and intended impact.

Team Workflow

Development Architecture

E=mc² + AI — Global Collaboration

Developed by an international team, Delta-Earth reflects the collaborative spirit of the NASA Space Apps Challenge: combining different perspectives and technical skills to make Earth observation more accessible.

From different parts of the world, we came together to explore one changing planet.
Our teammates are from the United States, India, Pakistan, and Peru!

Our Vision

Delta-Earth — Discover Earth's Changing Story.

Making satellite observations accessible, environmental changes understandable, and Earth science engaging for everyone.
